This document combines the agenda for a Special Meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, held March 18, 2014, at 6:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, with the supporting bid-award memo for its single business item: Network and Phone Purchase Approval under the 2014 Technology Bond.

The suggested resolution reads that the network and phone purchase be awarded to Hi-Tech, Inc. for the acquisition and installation of networking equipment from Extreme Networks for wired/wireless data systems and the acquisition and installation of telecommunications equipment from Shoretel, in the amount of $1,912,095, with that amount approved as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. The award is part of the district's Technology Bond Project for 2013/14, which planned to replace major components of the telephone, network security, and wired/wireless network.

A memo dated March 13, 2014, from Mark Washington, Director of Technology, to Dr. Barbara Fowler, Superintendent (subject: Bid Award Recommendation for Voice, Video, Security and Data Network; cc M. Rajter) explains the procurement. The district used two state-approved bid tools, the Midwest Higher Education Consortium (MHEC) and the Michigan Intercollegiate Telecommunications Consortium (MiCTA), to evaluate two vendors: Extreme Networks and Cisco Systems, the district's then-current network provider. After an in-depth analysis comparing product features, the bid from Hi-Tech, Inc. of Casco, Michigan, was recommended. Recent updates included a cost reduction of $304,248, making the recommendation $409,453 less than Cisco's most recent updated bid as of 3/5/14.

The bid summary shows Cisco's initial submission of 2/22/14 at $2,777,327 plus $327,334 installation for a $3,104,661 initial total (with voluntary alternates $2,446,795, revised total $2,774,129), versus the Extreme/Shoretel initial bid of $2,302,555 with installation included (voluntary alternates $2,127,581, revised total $2,216,343) - a difference of $557,786 in Extreme/Shoretel's favor. In the revised round, Cisco's updated bid as of 3/6/14 was $2,251,548 while Extreme/Shoretel was $1,912,095, both with installation included.

The memo lists benefits of the Extreme Networks solution: an enterprise-grade, fully redundant network core for faster traffic management; centralized network management console; traffic management at the access point; policy-based control of users and resources; wireless device data analytics; integration with the district content filter iBoss; district-wide wireless coverage; a Data Center Manager supporting the district's VMware environment; integrated Digital Citizenship enforcement; BYOD solutions differentiating guest and non-district devices; and coverage of all network-related costs for five years with a full warranty. Installation was to be completed by June 2014, and the bond funds allocated were within the project budget. The agenda structure lists Pledge of Allegiance, Public Communication, the business consideration, Other, and Adjournment, with the resolution left blank for mover, supporter, and vote tally.

This document is the 'Teaching & Learning Update' slide presentation delivered to the Troy School District Board of Education at its regular board meeting on September 15, 2015. It lays out the district's instructional framework and then focuses in detail on the rollout of the Schoology learning management system.

Teaching & Learning Focus: the deck names three organizing ideas - OneTroy, World Class District, and 'Do Less Better.' It quotes Fullan & Quinn's book 'Coherence' (2016): 'When large numbers of people have a deeply understood sense of what needs to be done and see their part in achieving that purpose, coherence emerges and powerful things happen.'

OneTroy Teaching & Learning Values are organized under three headings, each with three sub-values:
- Deepening Learning: Ambitious Outcomes for All; Engaged Learners; Innovative Practice.
- Focusing Direction: Continuous Reflection; Clarity of Strategy; Meaningful Goals.
- Cultivating a Collaborative Culture: Cooperative Decisions; Highly Effective Teams; Capacity Building.

The bulk of the presentation addresses Schoology and why the district adopted it. Stated reasons include: the ability to send information from any device to a central hub; assignments, assessments, and projects submitted from any device; a calendar to communicate upcoming assignments and important school events; integration with Office 365 and other apps; safe, secure class communication between students and teachers; the ability to embed audio and video within the site with unlimited storage for teachers; a common TSD learning management system with a single login and password; integration with iPad, smartphone, and PC devices; and an integrated gradebook with eSchools. The deck references a 1:44 promotional video from Larson Middle School and the site http://tsdschoology.weebly.com.

Under 'Schoology 2015-2016,' the district set out its operating expectations for the school year: major class assignments would be posted in Schoology; Schoology would be the preferred communication tool; the gradebook for Secondary would be Schoology; teachers would post all grades and the overall grade during the 4th, 7th, and 10th week of the marking periods; and there would be no official Secondary Interim Progress Report (the ongoing Schoology gradebook replacing the traditional interim report).

The presentation is informational and contains no dollar figures, contract parties, vote outcomes, or policy numbers; it documents the district's instructional vision and its shift to Schoology as the common learning management platform and secondary gradebook for the 2015-2016 school year.

This is the agenda, with supporting engagement letter, for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held Thursday, March 17, 2016, at 5:30 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Board meetings were cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

The agenda consisted of the Pledge of Allegiance, Public Communication, a Business item (consideration of a policy services provider, Lusk Albertson), a Closed Session (consideration of attorney-client privilege), and Adjournment.

The Business item recommended that the School District engage the law firm Lusk Albertson to assist in reviewing, preparing, and maintaining Board bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations. The suggested resolution read: "Be it therefore resolved that the Troy Board of Education engage the services of Lusk Albertson to assist in review, preparation and maintenance of Board bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations consistent with their submitted proposal dated March 8, 2016, in the amount not to exceed $15,000; and $4,000 annually for updates; and that these amounts be approved as an expenditure of the General Fund." The resolution included blanks for moving/supporting trustees and Yes/No votes; the outcome is not recorded in the text.

The packet includes a March 8, 2016 engagement letter (sent via email only) from Lusk Albertson to Mr. Rick West, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, signed with direct dial (248) 988-5695 and email KSutton@LuskAlbertson.com, regarding "Lusk Albertson Policy Service - Updated." The letter notes that the firm's representative met with the Board of Education on February 2, 2016 to discuss the service, and asks the District to counter-sign to confirm terms.

Under the engagement, Lusk Albertson (LA) would provide the District with a standard set of bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations that are more concise than the District's current version and that do not attempt to re-state the law (since the District must follow the law regardless of its policies). LA would deliver standard bylaws and policies upon engagement and expected to finish its standard administrative regulations by the end of that month, obtaining and incorporating input from the Board and Administration to finalize the documents.

Regarding copyrighting and branding, the District acknowledges LA's intellectual property rights; all bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations prepared by LA would be copyrighted and remain LA's property even if modified per District input, with the District holding a license to use them. The District would retain that license even if it later invokes the opt-out provision and discontinues its relationship with LA's School Policy Service, and agrees not to facilitate unauthorized use or sale of LA's documents; the final documents would include a visible text reference reflecting LA's ownership rights, presented in a manner LA would consult with the District about.

On cost, the letter specifies that the initial set of bylaws and policies costs $5,000.00, payable upon delivery, and the initial set of administrative regulations costs $10,000.00, payable upon delivery - flat fees that include whatever time LA attorneys need to obtain the necessary input from the Board and Administration to create the final complete sets.

The meeting closed with a consideration to enter closed session regarding attorney-client privilege, followed by adjournment.

Purpose
Procedural meeting to lawfully convene a closed session on a real-estate matter (Section 23 property sale) ahead of the same evening's organizational/regular meeting. No outcome recorded.

Special Meeting agenda for the Troy School District Board of Education, held January 17, 2017, at 6:30 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

The single substantive action is a resolution to enter closed session to discuss the sale of Section 23 property. The supporting text states the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss the sale, after which no additional business will take place other than to officially adjourn. The suggested resolution reads: "Be it therefore resolved that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss the sale of Section 23 property." A roll-call vote is indicated for board members Philippart, Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, and Miletti. This special meeting preceded the same evening's Organizational and Regular Meeting, whose regular business included a Section 23 Purchase Agreement.
